o: A salutation, and an account of saving blessings, as prepared in God's eternal election, as purchased by Christ's blood.
And as conveyed in effectual calling: this is applied to the believing Jews, and to the believing Gentiles.
The apostle thanks God for their faith and love, and prays for the continuance of their knowledge and hope, with respect to the heavenly inheritance, and to God's powerful working in them.
bg: Was written by Paul at Rome about the same time as that to the Colossians, which in many points it resembles.
ch.s: This chapter covers: A salutation, and an account of saving blessings, as prepared in God's eternal election, as purchased by Christ's blood (vv. 1–8); And as conveyed in effectual calling: this is applied to the believing Jews, and to the believing Gentiles (vv. 9–14); The apostle thanks God for their faith and love, and prays for the continuance of their knowledge and hope, with respect to the heavenly inheritance, and to God's powerful working in them (vv. 15–23). People named: Paul. Places: Ephesus.
ch.mh: All Christians must be saints; if they come not under that character on earth, they will never be saints in glory.
q: Read verses 1–8 (A salutation, and an account of saving blessings, as prepared in God's eternal election, as purchased by Christ's blood). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 9–14 (And as conveyed in effectual calling: this is applied to the believing Jews, and to the believing Gentiles), what do you learn about worship and praise?
Verse 4 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 2 Timothy 1:9. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Paul’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of faith and trust in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Ephesians?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: And did we know what we are called to, and what we might find in him, surely we should come and be suitors to him.
ch.a: Write down three things this chapter shows about God and thank Him for each.

o: The riches of God's grace towards men, shown from their deplorable state by nature, and the happy change Divine grace makes in them.
The Ephesians called to reflect on their state of heathenism.
And the privileges and blessings of the gospel.
bg: Was written by Paul at Rome about the same time as that to the Colossians, which in many points it resembles.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The riches of God's grace towards men, shown from their deplorable state by nature, and the happy change Divine grace makes in them (vv. 1–10); The Ephesians called to reflect on their state of heathenism (vv. 11–13); And the privileges and blessings of the gospel (vv. 14–22).
ch.mh: Sin is the death of the soul.
q: Read verses 1–10 (The riches of God's grace towards men, shown from their deplorable state by nature, and the happy change Divine grace makes in them). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?

ch.aq: Let us seek to discharge the duties allotted to us, to the glory of God.
ch.a: Show the same mercy you have received to someone who does not deserve it.

ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle sets forth his office, and his qualifications for it, and his call to it (vv. 1–7); Also the noble purposes answered by it (vv. 8–12); He prays for the Ephesians (vv. 13–19); And adds a thanksgiving (vv. 20,21). People named: Paul.
ch.mh: For having preached the doctrine of truth, the apostle was a prisoner, but a prisoner of Jesus Christ; the object of special protection and care, while thus suffering for him.
q: Read verses 1–7 (The apostle sets forth his office, and his qualifications for it, and his call to it). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?

Verse 20 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 2 Corinthians 9:8. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Paul’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of the church and fellowship in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Ephesians?

ch.aq: Let us expect more, and ask for more, encouraged by what Christ has already done for our souls, being assured that the conversion of sinners, and the comfort of believers, will be to his glory, for ever and ever.
ch.a: Show the same mercy you have received to someone who does not deserve it.

o: Exhortations to mutual forbearance and union.
To a due use of spiritual gifts and graces.

bg: Was written by Paul at Rome about the same time as that to the Colossians, which in many points it resembles.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Exhortations to mutual forbearance and union (vv. 1–6); To a due use of spiritual gifts and graces (vv. 7–16); To purity and holiness (vv. 17–24); And to take heed of the sins practised among the heathen (vv. 25–32).
ch.mh: Nothing is pressed more earnestly in the Scriptures, than to walk as becomes those called to Christ's kingdom and glory.
q: Read verses 1–6 (Exhortations to mutual forbearance and union). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 7–16 (To a due use of spiritual gifts and graces), what do you learn about the holy spirit?
Verse 22 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Romans 6:6. How do the two passages shed light on each other?

ch.aq: Wherever that blessed Spirit dwells as a Sanctifier, he is the earnest of all the joys and glories of that redemption day; and we should be undone, should God take away his Holy Spirit from us.
ch.a: Name one worry and deliberately hand it over to God in prayer each day this week.

o: Exhortation to brotherly love.

The duties of wives and husbands are enforced by the spiritual relation between Christ and the church.
bg: Was written by Paul at Rome about the same time as that to the Colossians, which in many points it resembles.

ch.mh: Because God, for Christ's sake, has forgiven you, therefore be ye followers of God, imitators of God.

o: The duties of children and parents.
Of servants and masters.
All Christians are to put on spiritual armour against the enemies of their souls.
The apostle desires their prayers, and ends with his apostolic blessing.
bg: Was written by Paul at Rome about the same time as that to the Colossians, which in many points it resembles.

Chance, an Asiatic Christian, a "faithful minister in the Lord" (Eph. 6:21, 22), who, with Trophimus, accompanied Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4). He is alluded to also in Col. 4:7, Titus 3:12, and 2 Tim. 4:12 as having been with Paul at Rome, whence he sent him to Ephesus, probably for the purpose of building up and encouraging the church there.

Jewish inhabitants. the conquests of Pompey seem to have given rise to the first settlement of Jews at Rome. The Jewish king Aristobulus and his son formed part of Pompey's triumph, and many Jewish captives and immigrants were brought to Rome at that time.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The duties of children and parents (vv. 1–4); Of servants and masters (vv. 5–9); All Christians are to put on spiritual armour against the enemies of their souls (vv. 10–18); The apostle desires their prayers, and ends with his apostolic blessing (vv. 19–24). People named: Tychicus, Rome.
ch.mh: The great duty of children is, to obey their parents.
q: Read verses 1–4 (The duties of children and parents). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 5–9 (Of servants and masters), what do you learn about prayer?
Verse 10 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Philippians 4:13. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Tychicus’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of faith and trust in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Ephesians?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us think upon these things, and continue our prayers with patience.
ch.a: Set aside a specific time this week to pray through this chapter's key verse.
